knowledge:
- key_parameters: method=Specifies the statistical method to use, either "frequency" (uses DNA concentration) or "prevalence" (compares presence/absence in negative controls vs. true samples) ;; conc=The name of the sample metadata column containing DNA concentration/quantitation data (required for the frequency method) ;; neg=The name of the sample metadata column (logical or name) indicating which samples are negative controls (required for the prevalence method) ;; threshold=The probability threshold for classifying a feature as a contaminant (default is 0.1; 0.5 is a more aggressive threshold for the prevalence method to identify sequences more prevalent in controls than in positive samples)
- alternatives: None mentioned ;; The documentation contrasts decontam with the common practice of sequencing negative controls and doing nothing, and mentions phyloseq for downstream data manipulation and pruning
- when_to_use: When analyzing environmental microbial communities, microbiomes, marker-gene (amplicon/16S rRNA), or shotgun metagenomics data, especially in low-biomass environments where contaminating DNA from reagents or extraction steps can critically interfere with downstream profiling
- pitfalls: Removing low-read samples too early: It is important to keep low-read samples (like negative controls) initially because they are crucial for identifying contaminants ;; Missing highly abundant contaminants with the prevalence method: Highly abundant contaminants might be present in almost all samples (both negative and positive) and thus missed by the prevalence method, whereas the frequency method can catch them ;; Not converting the negative control indicator to a logical variable (TRUE/FALSE) as required by the neg parameter in the prevalence method

workflows.name: frequency_based_decontamination
workflows.intent: Identify and remove contaminating sequence features based on the inverse relationship between their frequency and sample DNA concentration.
input: sample_data (metadata containing DNA concentration measurements, e.g., PicoGreen fluorescent intensity)
workflows.stages: 1. Load phyloseq object containing feature table and metadata ;; 2. Run frequency-based contaminant identification using isContaminant ;; 3. Visualize frequency vs. concentration using plot_frequency ;; 4. Filter out identified contaminants using prune_taxa
workflows.code:
library(phyloseq); packageVersion("phyloseq")
library(ggplot2); packageVersion("ggplot2")
library(decontam); packageVersion("decontam")
ps <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "MUClite.rds", package="decontam"))
contamdf.freq <- isContaminant(ps, method="frequency", conc="quant_reading")
head(contamdf.freq)
table(contamdf.freq$contaminant)
head(which(contamdf.freq$contaminant))
plot_frequency(ps, taxa_names(ps)[c(1,3)], conc="quant_reading") + 
  xlab("DNA Concentration (PicoGreen fluorescent intensity)")
ps.noncontam <- prune_taxa(!contamdf.freq$contaminant, ps)

workflows.name: prevalence_based_decontamination
workflows.intent: Identify and remove contaminating sequence features by comparing their presence/absence (prevalence) in true positive samples versus negative control samples.
input: sample_data (metadata identifying which samples are negative controls)
workflows.stages: 1. Load phyloseq object containing feature table and metadata ;; 2. Define a logical variable indicating negative control samples ;; 3. Run prevalence-based contaminant identification using isContaminant ;; 4. Optionally run with an aggressive threshold (e.g., 0.5) ;; 5. Visualize prevalence in positive vs. negative samples
workflows.code:
library(phyloseq); packageVersion("phyloseq")
library(ggplot2); packageVersion("ggplot2")
library(decontam); packageVersion("decontam")
ps <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "MUClite.rds", package="decontam"))
sample_data(ps)$is.neg <- sample_data(ps)$Sample_or_Control == "Control Sample"
contamdf.prev <- isContaminant(ps, method="prevalence", neg="is.neg")
table(contamdf.prev$contaminant)
head(which(contamdf.prev$contaminant))
contamdf.prev05 <- isContaminant(ps, method="prevalence", neg="is.neg", threshold=0.5)
table(contamdf.prev05$contaminant)
ps.pa <- transform_sample_counts(ps, function(abund) 1*(abund>0))
ps.pa.neg <- prune_samples(sample_data(ps.pa)$Sample_or_Control == "Control Sample", ps.pa)
ps.pa.pos <- prune_samples(sample_data(ps.pa)$Sample_or_Control == "True Sample", ps.pa)
df.pa <- data.frame(pa.pos=taxa_sums(ps.pa.pos), pa.neg=taxa_sums(ps.pa.neg),
                      contaminant=contamdf.prev$contaminant)
ggplot(data=df.pa, aes(x=pa.neg, y=pa.pos, color=contaminant)) + geom_point() +
  xlab("Prevalence (Negative Controls)") + ylab("Prevalence (True Samples)")
